title: Mathematics of Herding
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23992v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A herd of animals often follows a leader who sets the direction of travel. The leader sometimes turns unexpectedly and the followers reshuffle. Yet the herd regroups itself and stays coherent. Our work aims to understand the herding behavior mathematically. We construct a minimal discrete-time nonequilibrium dynamical system with one-way coupling, and the minimal structure allows an exact analysis. Take the location of each follower in the frame of the leader. The recorded locations form a distribution. The limit of the distribution is the asymptotic spatial measure, whose geometric representation we study. The dynamics of the herd have an exact operator representation with two factors, the operator of a fixed leader-follower pair and the operator of the interaction rules, which reshuffle the pairs. We show that the influence of the leader passes through some follower more than once. As a result, two followers can have reciprocal influence, despite the one-way coupling.

title: Extinction and the global structure of positive equilibria in a ratio-dependent intraguild predation model
abstract:
arXiv:2610.23995v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study an intraguild predation model with ratio-dependent trophic interactions. We first derive sufficient conditions for consumer extinction, total extinction, and global convergence to biologically relevant boundary equilibria. We then turn to coexistence at equilibrium and introduce a biologically motivated coordinate transformation that reduces the positive-equilibrium problem to an explicitly parameterized one-dimensional curve. This reduction enables us to determine how the positive-equilibrium branch connects to boundary equilibria and to classify all of its admissible global geometries. We also discuss the stability of positive equilibria. Numerical examples suggest the presence of periodic and chaotic coexistence, as well as several forms of multiple attractors.

title: An Unbounded Gap Between Identification and Identifiable Elicitation: Central Moments
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24009v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For $n\geq2$, two expectation equations identify the mean together with the $n$th central moment. How many coordinates must a report have if a one-observation loss uniquely elicits it and the report determines that moment? We prove that $n$ coordinates are necessary and sufficient among all identifiable intermediaries. The result holds on every open convex set of positive distributions on any $n+1$ distinct real outcomes. It requires no regularity of the loss, report map, identification function, or link. Thus $\operatorname{elic}_{\mathcal I}(\mu_n)=n$ while $\operatorname{iden}(\mu_n)\leq2$, giving an unbounded gap between identifiable elicitation and indirect identification. This resolves the central-moment conjecture of Frongillo and Kash on the stated domains. The proof constructs a $C^1$ manifold of supporting coefficients from the affine fibers of a convex negative Bayes risk. Translations along that manifold force an $n$-dimensional tangent space. Standardized moments of order at least three have the same exact complexity. The bound also extends to convex distribution classes with a full-dimensional raw-moment image.

title: Causal Information Exchange as a Necessary Condition for Adaptive Regulation: A Perturbational Framework for Life and Agency
authors: Brian LuValle, Abicumaran Uthamacumaran, Hector Zenil
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24017v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Information exchange can support living organisation without providing a sufficient criterion for life. We develop a perturbational framework that distinguishes causal transmission, directional imbalance, internal retention, response structure and functional regulation. Randomised interventions define Shannon information channels; for deterministic binary recipients, their context-conditioned mutual information is exactly a paired perturbation-response indicator. Spatial and temporal averages of these local channels measure information-exposure density, rather than joint information or conserved information flux. Complementary Coding Theorem Method and Block Decomposition Method (BDM) estimates describe response and trajectory structure. A same-shaped zero-mask reference separates raw BDM from a structural contrast; neither is a channel mutual information. Retained exploratory BDM plots are distinguished from the normalised causal-channel results. Retention-weighted coupling and directionality obey algebraic bounds, and ensemble reciprocity need not imply reciprocity within individual contexts. For a specified binary sensor--internal-channel--actuator task, we derive a positive information lower bound from successful regulation and construct controllers with identical information profiles but opposite functional outcomes. A study of 2,000 ordered elementary-cellular-automaton rule pairs, six detailed examples, recurrence and lossless coding analyses, and a signed-network extension demonstrates dissociations among perturbational responsiveness, structural regularity and recurrence. The results establish causal information as a necessary resource for the stated form of adaptive regulation, while showing why neither causal coupling nor response complexity alone measures agency or life.

title: Explicit construction of optimal binary linear complementary pairs via Belov codes
authors: Yansheng Wu, Jing Chen, Jong Yoon Hyun
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24019v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The study of linear complementary pairs (LCPs) has been a hot topic in coding theory. Recently, G\"uneri constructed an infinite family of optimal binary LCPs from Solomon-Stiffler codes. Specifically, he proved that for every $k \geq 5$ and $d \geq \lceil (k - 1)/2 \rceil 2^{k - 1}$, there exist optimal binary linear complementary pairs of codes of length $g_2(k,d)$, where $g_2(k,d)$ denotes the Griesmer bound.
  In this paper, we construct additional optimal binary LCPs from Belov codes, which form a generalized class of Solomon-Stiffler codes. Our results not only generalize G\"uneri's construction, but also enable more flexible construction of optimal binary LCPs with a wide range of minimum distances.

title: A Note on Carmichael Numbers of the form $ N=(d+1)(3d+1)(4d+1)$
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24042v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study integers of the form
  \[ N=(d+1)(3d+1)(4d+1). \] Using Korselt's criterion, we prove that, provided the three factors are prime, $N$ is a Carmichael number if and only if \[ d\equiv4\pmod{12}. \]
  We also show that the special case $d=2^m$ produces only $1105$ under the prime-factor hypothesis.

title: Dynamic Control of a Make-to-Order Manufacturing System under Throughput Time Constraints: An Effective Computational Method in the High-Dimensional Case
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24096v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider dynamic control of a make-to-order production system that serves price- and delay-sensitive customers. The production system is modeled as a multiclass queueing network where the customers' delay sensitivity is modeled via throughput-time constraints. To maximize her profit while meeting these throughput time constraints, the system manager uses three different types of control: i) dynamic pricing decisions; ii) dynamic order-of-service (scheduling) decisions; and iii) outsourcing decisions upon arrival of new orders. We approximate this problem by a multi-dimensional Brownian control problem in heavy traffic, and develop a neural network-based computational method tailored for high-dimensional problems. By interpreting the solution in the context of the original model, we propose an integrated dynamic pricing, outsourcing, and scheduling policy. The effectiveness of this policy is demonstrated through a simulation study of two test problems drawn from the literature.

title: Singular Aubry--Mather Sets for a Homogeneous Single-Input Control System
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24145v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop an Aubry--Mather theory for the abnormal arcs of a time-minimal single-input affine control system in dimension three with homogeneous cubic drift. We show that the Bonnard--Kupka semi-invariant defining the abnormal locus is a Darboux polynomial of the desingularized singular field, with an explicit cofactor; this gives the invariance of the abnormal locus, a closed formula for the multiplier of its periodic components and, through the antipodal symmetry of the model, their description as lifts of ovals of a real plane quintic. For a compact invariant set of a singular flow we then define a singular Aubry--Mather structure, whose Lagrangian is supported on the graph of the singular field and whose Hamilton--Jacobi equation is linear in the momentum. We prove a duality formula for the critical value, the existence of critical subsolutions strict outside the Aubry set, and the covariance of the structure under time changes. On the abnormal locus the structure selects the periodic components of minimal average cost, governs transverse stability, and exhibits a sharp obstruction to correctors along heteroclinic cycles; for the radial exponent of the homogeneous dynamics, the corrector is the periodic part of the logarithmic radius. An explicit cubic example illustrates the results.

title: Geometric Stability of Dynamical Systems with Self-Generated State-Space Memory
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24152v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop a geometric stability framework for dynamical systems coupled to memory fields generated by their own state trajectories. Temporal age and state-space displacement enter a nonlinear hereditary force admitting an exact, trajectory-dependent velocity representation. A common velocity-history phase space contains both resting and uniformly translating solutions. We establish global velocity arrest under a uniform geometric memory-gain bound and obtain exact translating-speed balance laws from the full radial imprint. The response slope yields a positive longitudinal exponent on rising-speed branches, while a complementary contraction criterion gives local exponential attraction to selected descending branches in the scalar velocity dynamics, in fading-memory topology. Our principal result is a constructive geometric non-identifiability theorem: two systems with identical nonlinear force operators on an open neighborhood of rest can exhibit sharply different complete-motion behavior at the same subcritical gain. In the first, every admissible trajectory with bounded velocity prehistory comes to rest exponentially; in the second, locally attracting rest coexists with a locally attracting translating branch and an additional spectrally unstable translating branch. The infinite-memory case exhibits exponentially flat force differences, with all finite-order equilibrium derivatives agreeing despite the possibility of distinct global translating families. The framework also yields classical Volterra kernels and distributed-derivative transfer functions by linearization.

title: Reusable QUBO-Derived Block-Schur Inverse Factors for Fixed-Operator Finite-Difference PDE Solvers
authors: Arash Fath Lipaei, \"Ozg\"ur E. M\"ustecapl{\i}o\u{g}lu, \"Ozlem Salehi, Selin Aslan
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24158v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many simulations of partial differential equations require the repeated solution of linear systems whose matrix remains fixed while the righthand side changes. We present a hybrid offline online framework for this setting. The discretized operator is organized into small coupled blocks and reduced through block Schur complements. Instead of expressing the complete PDE solution as one large binary optimization problem, quadratic unconstrained binary optimization is used only to construct reusable local inverse factors. These factors are computed during an offline stage, decoded and stored, and then reused in an ordinary classical block solve for subsequent righthand sides. The optimizer facing problem size is governed by the local block size and chosen numerical precision, rather than by the dimension of the full spatial grid. We develop the mathematical formulation, analyze the accuracy and resource requirements of the binary representation, and examine the method on representative finite difference PDE problems, including execution of the local optimization stage on quantum optimization hardware. The resulting architecture provides a reusable interface between conventional numerical linear algebra and QUBO based quantum optimization.

title: Explicit Criteria for Finite-Time Identification in Sparse Primal--Dual Dynamics
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24163v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study when selected coordinates become and remain zero in a finite-dimensional sparse-regression primal--dual flow and its exact full resolvent iteration. Invariant balls centered at \((0,z)\), with \(z\) strictly dual feasible, give computable deadlines without rank assumptions or optimizer knowledge. The certificates may be available at initialization. We determine the smallest invariant radius for the continuous flow within this family. For a prescribed positive feasibility margin, center selection is convex and admits an exact finite conic formulation. We bound the coordinate margins for all centers in this family and give a normalized correlated example attaining the bound. A composite Bregman Lyapunov estimate proves rank-free convergence without primal uniqueness and finite identification under strict dual margins. Under restricted injectivity, the discrete gap-based deadlines multiplied by the step size tend to the continuous bound for fixed data, observed state, and certificate parameters. Numerical experiments assess certificate timing. A noisy weak-form oscillator regression illustrates the difference between fitted and physical support.

title: On condensations of $C_p(X)$ spaces onto Banach spaces with the weak topology
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24165v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We show that for a broad class of spaces $X$, the space $C_p(X)$ of continuous real-valued functions on $X$ equipped with the pointwise topology maps bijectively onto any separable infinite-dimensional Banach space with the weak topology. We prove that the inverse $\varphi^{-1}$ of any continuous bijection $\varphi: C_p(X)\to (E,w)$, where $X$ is an arbitrary infinite Tychonoff space and $(E,w)$ is an arbitrary normed space with the weak topology, is everywhere discontinuous. This generalizes a recent result of Kania--K\k{a}kol and solves a problem raised by K\k{a}kol, Leiderman and Michalak by providing a complete classification of function spaces $C_p(X)$ that are homeomorphic to Banach spaces with the weak topology.

title: Representing Information on DNA using Patterns Induced by Enzymatic Labeling
authors: Daniella Bar-Lev, Eitan Yaakobi, Zohar Yakhini, Tuvi Etzion
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24171v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Enzymatic DNA labeling is a powerful tool with applications in biochemistry, molecular biology, biotechnology, medical science, and genomic research. This paper contributes to the evolving field of DNA-based data storage by presenting a formal framework for modeling DNA labeling in strings, specifically tailored for data storage purposes. Our approach involves a known DNA molecule as a template for labeling, employing patterns induced by a set of designed labels to represent information. One hypothetical implementation can use CRISPR-Cas9 and gRNA reagents for labeling. Various aspects of the general labeling channel, including fixed-length labels, are explored, and upper bounds on the maximum size of the corresponding codes are given. The study includes the development of an efficient encoder-decoder pair that is proven to be optimal in terms of maximum code size under specific conditions.
  The codewords for this framework are codesets, i.e., each codeword is a collection of a few labels. Of special interest are codes whose codesets contain fixed-length labels. Their construction and analysis are tied to de Bruijn sequences and constrained coding.

title: Certifiably Correct Fr\'echet Means in Orbit Spaaces
authors: Dustin G. Mixon, Tom Needham, Nathan Willey
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24191v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study Fr\'echet means in orbit spaces of finite orthogonal group actions. Since computing these means is NP-hard in general, we take inspiration from group synchronization to develop tractable spectral and semidefinite relaxations. Pairwise alignment certifies global optimality and we develop a semidefinite certificate that can extend beyond this condition. For Gaussian data modulo sign, we prove that our certificate succeeds in a high-noise regime where alignment fails. Numerical experiments evaluate these methods in various settings, including summarizing ensembles of districting plans and clustering time series

title: Certified neural approximations for parabolic obstacle problems
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24202v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Residual-trained neural surrogates carry no error guarantee, a limitation for free-boundary problems such as phase change and contact. We derive guaranteed error bounds for neural approximations of parabolic obstacle problems in first-order state--flux--multiplier form. The main result bounds the flux error of the network and the energy error of its feasible projection $\max\{v,g\}$ by the constitutive residual, the initial mismatch, the complementarity defect, and the PDE residual weighted by $c_F^2/\alpha$, without the coercivity and norm-equivalence constants of the first-order formulation. It extends the Apushkinskaya--Repin majorant for the heat operator to general coefficients, free multipliers and a flux bound. A penetration-consistency result shows that neural triples with arbitrarily small bound exist. Outward-rounded cellwise Taylor-model enclosures turn the bound into a finite computation valid on any adaptive partition. The flux and gradient errors of the projected output are certified below $0.27$ and $0.33$ of the solution scale for a one-dimensional Stefan problem and, after adaptive refinement, below one half for all three trained networks on a two-dimensional expanding disk. On an expanding ellipse the gradient bound stays above one half; substitution diagnostics trace the floor of the trained networks to the projected state near the free boundary, and the remaining gap to enclosure overhead. Without a closed-form solution, a validated lower bound replaces the solution norm; there the enclosure is nearly exact, but the trained networks have errors above the solution scale and no useful accuracy is certified. The bounds control a state--flux norm, not the multiplier or the free-boundary location.

title: Orientation Diversity Provably Increases the Angular-Domain Rank of 3D MIMO Arrays
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24228v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Movable and rotatable-antenna systems treat element placement as a design resource, but the supporting theory is largely position-only. We prove that element orientation is an effective spatial resource in its own right, complementary to position. For collinear or coplanar arrays, the angular-domain rank is capped by the number of projection-ambiguity classes of the scattering directions, for every common element orientation and pattern. Orientation-diverse elements with sufficiently rich analytic patterns restore the maximal rank min(N,L) for almost every orientation draw. A closed-form correlation expression, strictly monotone in orientation spread under isotropic scattering, quantifies the gain within the scalar-pattern model, and Monte Carlo simulations corroborate the exact-rank and capacity behavior.

title: Pilot-Projected Nonlinear Self-Interference Estimation with Simultaneous Uplink Training
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24243v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper considers nonlinear digital self-interference (SI) cancellation and uplink-channel estimation for single-antenna in-band full-duplex radios when a desired uplink pilot is present during SI training. In this setting, a rich nonlinear SI dictionary can absorb part of the structured pilot response, while its large and correlated set of basis functions can make reliable SI estimation difficult, particularly with limited training. During SI-coefficient estimation, we treat the unknown uplink channel as a nuisance parameter and eliminate it to obtain an equivalent reduced SI estimation problem on the orthogonal complement of the pilot convolution subspace. Since the projected nonlinear dictionary can remain ill conditioned, we develop two complementary full-dictionary estimators: a pilot-projected ridge estimator with Bayesian-information-criterion tuning (PP-RidgeBIC), which uses global ridge shrinkage, and a pilot-projected group-sparse Bayesian estimator (PP-GSBE), which learns branch-dependent Bayesian shrinkage from the data. These estimators offer two complementary operating points: PP-RidgeBIC favors computational efficiency, whereas PP-GSBE provides greater adaptivity to heterogeneous nonlinear SI components. Simulations show substantial gains in SI cancellation and uplink reception over non-projected and hard-selection alternatives; notably, PP-GSBE suppresses the residual SI below the noise floor with moderate training and consistently provides the strongest performance under nonlinear model mismatch.

title: Build Your Own Neural Network From Scratch
authors: Samantha Donner, Ethan Geary, Peter March, Mathew Umano
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24271v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: These notes are based on our reading of Michael Nielsen's online book neuralnetworksanddeeplearning.com. They represent our effort to elaborate his exposition of neural networks and to provide supporting mathematical detail. Our goal is to provide self-contained instructions for building a basic neural network in the form of pseudocode, so that an interested reader can build a network from scratch and know why it works. No prior knowledge of neural networks or of Python is assumed. Some familiarity with linear algebra, calculus, and probability is helpful but we explain the relevant mathematics in a set of appendices designed to be accessible to newcomers.

title: Two-parameter Toeplitz-type operators between Fock spaces
authors: Xingtang Dong, Zipeng Wang, Kehe Zhu
abstract: arXiv:2610.24318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and study a two-parameter family of Toeplitz-type operators $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi$ on the Fock space $F^p(C)$ for $0

title: Computing Multi-Slot First-Price Pacing Equilibria at Scale via Entropic Smoothing
authors: Yuchen Xie, Shenyinying Tu, Yuan Gao, Yi Zhang, Deepak Kumar
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24323v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Pacing equilibria describe how budget-constrained advertisers clear an ad market, but computing one at production scale is hard when every request fills several slots: the allocation jumps whenever two campaigns' scores cross. We consider the first-price pacing equilibrium (FPPE) of auctions with $K$ homogeneous slots and unit-demand campaigns, whose Eisenberg-Gale dual reduces, via a TopK identity, to a convex program over bids. Regularizing each request's allocation with the binary (Fermi-Dirac) entropy gives a smooth, strictly convex dual whose gradient is exactly spend minus budget and whose evaluation splits into independent one-dimensional threshold solves, one per request. The smoothed equilibrium converges to the hard one at an explicit $O(\sqrt{T})$ rate, and a duality gap certifies how far any bids are from the hard equilibrium. We implement an efficient multi-GPU solver and test it on a production ad workload. We use it to compute an equilibrium price anchor: each campaign's hindsight equilibrium cost per key result.

title: Minimality of $T_z^*$-Invariant Subspaces of $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$
authors: Jo\~ao Marcos R. do Carmo, Marcos S. Ferreira
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24327v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we establish necessary conditions for the minimality of infinite-dimensional $T_z^*$-invariant subspaces of $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$. More precisely, we prove that if $M\subset H^2(\mathbb D^2)$ is an infinite-dimensional, minimal $T_z^*$-invariant subspace, then, for every $n\in\mathbb N_0$, either $\overline{P_n(M)}=H^2(\mathbb D)$ or $\overline{P_n(M)}^\perp =\phi_{a,\theta}H^2(\mathbb D)$ where $\phi_{a,\theta}$ is an atomic singular inner function and $P_n$ denotes the orthogonal projection of $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$ onto $H^2(z)w^n$. As $T_z^*$ is a universal operator on $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$, this result reduces the Invariant Subspace Problem to the analysis of these two alternatives for infinite-dimensional minimal $T_z^*$-invariant subspaces.

title: Benign Overfitting Property of the Minimum $\ell_q$ -norm Interpolant Estimator in Regression Problem via Feature Space Decomposition
authors: Rados{\l}aw Adamczak, Guillaume Lecu\'e, Zong Shang, Marta Strzelecka
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24350v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper establishes high-probability, non-asymptotic upper bounds for the population excess risk of minimum $\ell_q$-norm interpolating estimators in linear regression, valid for all $1<q><\infty$ under three scenarios: convex concentration, mild moment assumptions and log-concavity. Consequently, we derive sufficient conditions for these estimators to exhibit benign overfitting. Our analysis hinges on a Feature Space Decomposition (FSD) framework, which naturally highlights the self-regularizing properties of minimum norm interpolants as well as the role of alignment between the signal and the features for benign overfitting. From a technical perspective, our approach circumvents the traditionally used Convex Gaussian Min-max Theorem (CGMT) by instead leveraging the Dvoretzky-Milman theorem. We emphasize that the FSD method has the potential to refine standard uniform convergence approaches. Furthermore, the isomorphic Dvoretzky-Milman theorem established herein -- proven under the three scenarios mentioned above -- for the $\ell_q$-norm is of independent mathematical interest.

title: Global stability of Michaelis-Menten networks
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24351v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In a very nice paper, Blanchini, Breda, Giordano and Liessi studied networks of species coupled through Michaelis-Menten interactions. Under standard assumptions of strong connectedness and non-degeneracy, they show that there is a unique equilibrium, which is (locally) asymptotically stable. This note shows that global stability, which was stated there as an open problem, holds as well. In fact, whenever a positive equilibrium exists, it attracts every solution with positive initial condition, with no connectedness or non-degeneracy hypothesis at all; those assumptions are needed only in order to guarantee existence and to cover solutions starting on the boundary of the orthant. The key is to note that the system is contractive with respect to the Thompson part metric.

title: Spherical-Design Oracles for Zeroth-Order Optimisation: Deterministic, Variance-Free Gradient Estimation
authors: Amir Ali Farzin, Yuen-Man Pun, Philipp Braun, Iman Shames
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24373v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this work, we develop a zeroth-order (ZO) method that estimates the gradient with minimal bias and variance. Instead of the random directions often used in the ZO literature, we consider central differences with directions given by a fixed spherical $t$-design, a finite point set that integrates every polynomial of degree at most $t$ exactly. The oracle is deterministic and thus does not induce any variance.We also propose a general finite difference method in the higher-order-smoothness regime and show the bias of both finite difference methods. We then show the convergence of the proposed ZO method via the input-to-state stability concept. Numerical experiments show the superiority of our proposed method over the existing random ZO methods.

title: Coactions of weak multiplier Hopf algebras
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24406v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this article, we investigate the notion of a coaction for a weak multiplier Hopf algebra. We show that there is a duality for actions and coactions of weak algebraic quantum groups. Then we obtain the well known Blattner-Montgomery duality theorem for weak algebraic quantum groups in the framework of dual pairs. We form a Morita context when the weak multiplier Hopf algebra admits a two-sided faithful integral and show that the coaction is Galois if and only if the map in the Morita context is surjective. As an application, we obtain the result that a grading by any groupoid $G$ can be considered as a $\mathrm{C}G$-comodule algebra. We also construct a Morita context connecting the smash product $A\# \mathrm{C}(G)$ and the coinvariant subalgebra $A^{\mathrm{C}(G)}$. Finally we construct an isomorphism between $(R\# \mathrm{C}(G))\# \mathrm{C}G$ and $R\otimes (\mathrm{C}(G)\# \mathrm{C}G)$ when $R$ is graded by $G$.

title: Asymptotic Normality of the Hill Estimator in Linear Preferential Attachment
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24413v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove asymptotic normality of the Hill estimator based on the largest $k_n$ degrees in a homogeneous linear preferential attachment graph with $n$ vertices. Each new vertex sends a fixed number $m\ge1$ of edges sequentially to older vertices, with attachment weight $d+\delta$ and fixed $\delta>-m$. Let $\alpha=m/(2m+\delta)$. For every deterministic sequence $k_n\to\infty$ satisfying $\sqrt{k_n}(k_n/n)^\alpha\to0$, the estimator, centered at $\alpha$ and multiplied by $\sqrt{k_n}$, converges to a centered normal law with an explicit variance strictly smaller than $\alpha^2$. The reduction relative to the Hill variance for independent observations separates into contributions from the different degree laws at different birth times and from competition for new edges. The contribution from competition is $1/m$ times that from different birth times. Representations using Gamma and beta functions give a consistent standard error and a studentized normal limit. The proof uses martingales indexed by edge attachments and comparisons with independent pure-birth processes, while retaining the integer degrees and their ties.

title: Certified Fourier rounding for the real Grothendieck inequality
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24417v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that the real Grothendieck constant is strictly smaller than $1.77987164$. The proof provides a complete interval-arithmetic realization of Ren's five-variable construction. A finite Fourier calculation encloses every scalar coefficient through degree $403$; a fourth-derivative estimate on the entire unit circle bounds the remaining coefficient sum by $10^{-4}$. Exact rational arithmetic then certifies the final inequality. We include the transfer to all finite real matrices and arbitrary vector dimensions, the analytic quadrature errors, the rational parameters, and source code for checking and regenerating the certificate.

title: A note on the rectangular Schoenberg-Whitney theorem for clamped B-splines
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24425v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Wang et al.(Computer-Aided Design 40 (2008) 999-1008) proposed a knot-subsequence characterization of full row rank for rectangular B-spline collocation matrices. We identify an incorrect inequality in their Appendix proof, which invalidates the argument as written, and make explicit the endpoint and multiplicity conventions on which the criterion depends. The defect lies in the proof, not in the underlying result, which is valid under suitably stated hypotheses; in the lofting construction of Wang et al. these hypotheses are implicitly satisfied, so the lofted curves are unaffected. We state the corrected result and give a new proof, independent of the disputed argument, for clamped B-splines of arbitrary degree with continuous interior multiplicities. In our proof, sufficiency follows from inclusion of spline spaces and knot insertion; necessity selects independent columns and builds the reduced knot vector from them. The proof uses no recursive column-selection construction.

title: Asymptotics for the number of saddle connections on a slit torus
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24429v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider a flat torus with a marked line segment $\beta$ and prove linear asymptotics for closed curves on the torus disjoint from the interior of the line segment. We also consider segments that begin and terminate at the end points of $\beta$ whose interiors are disjoint from $\beta$ and prove $L\log L$ asymptotics. In all cases, after quotienting by the growth rate, we compute the constant explicitly, which differs depending on whether or not $\beta$ lies in a periodic direction on the torus. In particular, when $\beta$ lies along a non-periodic trajectory, we show the constant is $2/(|\beta| \zeta(2))$. Moreover, we prove that as a function of the holonomy vector of $\beta$, the constants are continuous at the points where $\beta$ lies in a non-periodic direction.

title: Dynamic Programming for Value-at-risk Markov Decision Processes in Continuous Spaces
authors: Xian Chen, Erick Delage, Weikai Wang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24439v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Value-at-Risk (VaR) is a widely adopted quantile-based risk measure in practice, yet incorporating VaR objectives into Markov decision processes (VaR MDPs) remains a longstanding challenge. Recent work has derived dynamic programming equations for VaR MDPs in finite state and action spaces but left the case of more general spaces unresolved. This paper establishes, for the first time, the validity of these equations in continuous spaces, for both finite- and infinite-horizon settings. Such cases naturally arise in many real-world dynamic decision-making problems. As an application, we study an optimal execution problem with a VaR objective and demonstrate that our framework enables the characterization of optimal dynamic strategies, resolving an open question in the field.

title: A new class of pyramidal central configurations for spatial Newtonian 6-body problems
authors: Liang Ding, Jin Wang, Jinrong Wang, Zhifu Xie
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24445v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While a non-concyclic rhombus can support a central configuration in the planar Newtonian four-body problem, such a configuration cannot serve as the base of a pyramidal central configuration in the spatial five-body problem. In this paper, we establish the existence of a new class of pyramidal central configurations in the spatial Newtonian six-body problem, characterized by a non-concyclic quadrilateral base. This geometric structure distinguishes the new configurations from the known pyramidal central configurations of the spatial five-body problem. We investigate several fundamental properties of these configurations and provide numerical examples illustrating the theoretical results in each case. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this new class of central configurations can be used to construct perverse solutions in three-dimensional space, revealing an additional connection between the geometry of central configurations and the dynamics of the Newtonian $N$-body problem.

title: A Crawling Metric on the Space of Subtrees of a Tree
authors: Thu-Le Tran, Cao Minh Quang, Nguyen Chi Tam, Kien Trung Nguyen
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24448v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose a crawling metric on the space of subtrees of a tree. The symmetric difference cannot tell whether two disjoint subtrees are close or far; we halve it and add the gap between them. The result is a metric, one half is the smallest factor, and the tree embeds canonically. The metric equals the least cost of crawling between subtrees by growing and shrinking without jumping. With simultaneous growth and shrinkage, subtrees of fixed length form a geodesic space.

title: A Gauge-Invariant Finite Element Method for the Time-Dependent Ginzburg--Landau Equations
authors: Huadong Gao, Yuhui Huang, Wen Xie
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24470v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: It is well known that the Ginzburg--Landau equations are gauge invariant. The
  most popular gauge choice in practical simulations is the temporal gauge, also
  known as the zero electric potential gauge. However, the commonly used
  N\'ed\'elec approximations may produce spurious giant vortices on domains with
  re-entrant corners. To address this issue while retaining the N\'ed\'elec
  approximation, we propose a finite element scheme that preserves the gauge
  invariance of the time-dependent Ginzburg--Landau equations at the discrete
  level. Under the temporal gauge, the method employs lowest-order N\'ed\'elec
  edge elements for the magnetic potential and continuous piecewise-linear
  elements for the order parameter on triangular and tetrahedral meshes, and
  yields a linear, decoupled formulation that requires only the solution of
  linear systems at each time step. We prove that the scheme is gauge invariant,
  preserves a discrete maximum bound principle for the order parameter,
  $\|\psi_h^n\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\le 1$, and satisfies a discrete energy law under mild step-size and
  mesh conditions. Numerical experiments confirm these theoretical properties.
  In particular, on domains with re-entrant corners, the scheme computes the
  correct physical solution, whereas conventional temporal-gauge discretizations
  with N\'ed\'elec elements produce an unphysical solution.

title: Zero-trace index of matrices
authors: Kennett L. Dela Rosa, Eloise P. Misa
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24486v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The zero-trace index $t(A)$ of a square complex matrix $A$ is introduced. It is defined as the largest integer $k$ such that $A$ admits a $k \times k$ compression with trace zero. This concept is analogous to the zero-dilation index $d(A)$ and is closely related to the $k$-numerical range. The $k$-numerical range is characterized as an intersection of half-planes, which is used to derive a formula for $t(A)$ that reduces its computation to the Hermitian case. Conditions for $t(A) = d(A)$ are also established, and matrices satisfying $t(A) = n - 1$ are characterized. Finally, the zero-trace index is determined for several classes of matrices.

title: Riemannian Submersion whose Total Manifold admits an Almost Hyperbolic Ricci Soliton
authors: Sonali Jaiswal, Akhilesh Yadav, S. S. Shukla
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24488v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In the present paper, we investigate geometric properties of a Riemannian submersion for which the total manifold is endowed with hyperbolic and almost hyperbolic Ricci solitons. We establish conditions under which the fibers of the submersion admit hyperbolic and almost hyperbolic Ricci solitons. Further, we derive necessary conditions for the base manifold to be an Einstein and a hyperbolic Ricci soliton. Also, we determine the scalar curvature associated with the fibers and the base manifold. Moreover, when the total space admits an almost hyperbolic Ricci soliton with a torse-forming potential vector field, we obtain conditions ensuring that the extrinsic vertical and horizontal distributions are almost generalized quasi-Einstein. We also obtain necessary conditions for the fibers and base manifold to be an Einstein and almost generalized quasi-Einstein manifold. Finally, examples are included to illustrate the existence of hyperbolic and almost hyperbolic Ricci solitons in Riemannian submersion.

title: The Segal-Bargmann Transform in Neural Partial Differential Equations
authors: Jie Xu, Julio Castrill\'on-Cand\'as, Mark Kon, Qinxun Bai
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24497v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce a novel neural operator method based on Segal-Bargmann transform and Bargmann-Fock space for learning the solution operators of partial differential equations (PDEs). The method brings data encoding, latent-space representation, operator learning, and decoding into an unifed framework. From only finitely many observations, we establish a sup-norm reconstruction error of order $ L^{-\frac{1}{2}} $, where L is the number of complex sampling points that are decoupled with the original samplings and observations. The reconstruction error is independent of the spatial dimension and the number of original sampling points. We show that this new mesh-free Segal-Bargmann Neural Operator approach has superior performance compared to existing NO approaches like FNO, BelNet, GNOT, etc.,\ particularly in terms of pointwise control $ \sup_{x}\lvert\hat{u}_{NO} - u_{truth}\rvert $ for solutions of PDEs $ \mathcal{L}u = f $ which provides pointwise accuracy and interpretability as classical numerical solvers. We also demonstrates the reconstructions of the solution operators for higher dimensional nonlinear PDEs, which suggest that our proposed method has great potential to be applied to more challenging PDEs and to even higher spatial dimensions.

title: Skew-Symmetric Formulations and Energy-Stable Schemes for Compressible Reactive Flow Equations
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24524v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper develops skew-symmetric formulations and energy stable finite difference schemes for the reactive Euler and reactive Navier--Stokes equations. By introducing suitable transformed variables, we rewrite the governing equations into skew-symmetric forms and obtain continuous energy estimates by standard integration-by-parts arguments. The proposed formulations extend the skew-symmetric framework for compressible flow equations to reactive systems, where the chemical energy and the species equation must be incorporated into the transformed variables. Based on these formulations, we construct semi-discrete schemes with summation-by-parts (SBP) operators. The convective terms are discretized by the non-dissipative part of linear upwind SBP operators, while a nonlinear SBP--WENO operator is used only to supply artificial dissipation near discontinuities. For periodic boundary conditions, the resulting schemes satisfy semi-discrete energy estimates consistent with the continuous analysis. Numerical experiments in one and two space dimensions validate the designed order of accuracy and demonstrate stable performance for problems with shocks, viscous layers, detonation-type waves, and complex wave interactions.

title: Analysis and approximation for inverse potential problem of space-dependent variable-exponent sub-diffusion in heterogeneous medium
authors: Zhiyuan Li, Chunlong Sun, Xiangcheng Zheng
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24531v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Anomalous transport in complex heterogeneous medium is often characterized by non-Markovian memory effects and spatially varying trapping properties. From the point of view of continuous-time random walks, such heterogeneity can be described by a position-dependent heavy-tailed waiting-time density $q(t \mid x)\sim C(x)t^{-1-\alpha(x)}$, where $0<\alpha(x)<1$ is the local anomalous exponent. This microscopic interpretation naturally leads to the sub-diffusion with a space-dependent variable exponent $\alpha(x)$. Compared with constant-exponent models, the variable-exponent fractional operators generally do not commute with the spatial Laplacian, which makes both the forward and inverse analysis substantially more delicate. This paper investigates the inverse problem of recovering a spatially dependent radiative or potential coefficient in variable-exponent sub-diffusion from terminal observation data. We formulate the inverse problem as a nonlinear fixed-point equation and prove that the associated fixed-point operator is monotone such that the fixed-point iteration converges decreasingly to the unique solution. We further establish a Lipschitz-type conditional stability estimate for the terminal observation map, which also implies uniqueness of the inverse problem for sufficiently large terminal time. For numerical reconstruction, we develop a fully discrete finite element scheme and derive an error estimate for the inverse problem. Numerical simulations are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the method, even in the presence of noisy data.

title: Extension of surjective isometries between unit spheres of $\ell^p$-direct sums
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24533v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study surjective isometries between the unit spheres of Banach spaces of the form $A\oplus_p B$, where $A$ is nonzero and strictly convex, $1

<\infty$, and every unit vector of $B\neq\{0\}$ has at least two distinct unit vectors at distance $2$. For two direct sums $A_i\oplus_{p_i}B_i$, $i=1,2$, satisfying these hypotheses, we prove that every surjective isometry $$\Delta:S_{A_1\oplus_{p_1}B_1}\to S_{A_2\oplus_{p_2} B_2}$$ between their unit spheres forces equality of the direct-sum exponents $p_i$ and extends uniquely to a surjective real-linear isometry $$\widetilde{\Delta}:A_1\oplus_p B_1\to A_2\oplus_p B_2$$ preserving the corresponding components, where $p:=p_1=p_2$. The proof identifies the component unit spheres through diametral sets and distance formulas, and then constructs isometries between the component unit balls. As a principal application, we obtain extension and representation results for absolutely continuous functions equipped with norms combining evaluation at a fixed point and the $L^1$-norm of the derivative. We also discuss Lipschitz and differentiable function spaces, distinguishing the consequences of our theorem from those already covered by existing extension results. Endpoint conclusions are derived separately, including the Mazur-Ulam property for the real absolutely continuous space with the sum norm.

title: Accelerating Finite-Sum Bilevel Optimization with Fully First-Order Oracles
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24538v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study nonconvex--strongly-convex bilevel optimization with finite-sum objectives and fully first-order oracles. We propose Sampled Implicit Corrections for Bilevel Optimization (SICBO), which combines a penalty approximation with variance-reduced corrections for the lower-level variables. Under componentwise lower strong convexity, SICBO finds a point $x$ satisfying $\mathbb{E}\|\nabla\Phi(x)\|^2\le\varepsilon^2$ within $\tilde{O}(N+\sqrt{N}\kappa^{7/2}\varepsilon^{-2})$ component-gradient calls, where $N$ is the total number of components and $\kappa$ is the normalized lower-level condition number. The bound achieves square-root finite-sum dependence using only gradients and preserves the best known deterministic fully first-order condition-number exponent for smooth problems. Our improvement follows from a curvature-dependent bound for nonlinear correction errors, which permits epochs of length $\tilde{\Theta}(\sqrt{N/\kappa})$ with batches of size $\tilde{\Theta}(\sqrt{N\kappa})$. A single-level reduction shows that the dependence on $N$ and $\varepsilon$ is optimal up to logarithmic factors for fixed $\kappa$.

title: Comment on "The polarization hierarchy for polynomial optimization over convex bodies, with applications to nonnegative matrix rank"
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24542v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We revisit the feasibility and convergence claims for the polarization hierarchy of Pl\'avala, Ligthart and Gross [Linear Algebra Appl.\ 723 (2025) 15--32]. Counterexamples show that the stated assumption is insufficient for the feasibility characterization and for convergence of the hierarchy with the polarization constraint. We establish corrected results under a stronger algebraic condition and supply a missing compactness argument.

title: Commutative exact superalgebras and super-modular tensor categories
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24568v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We extend the theory of commutative exact algebras in braided finite tensor categories (Shimizu-Yadav) to superalgebras, motivated by extensions of vertex operator (super)algebras.
  For a braided category $\C$ let $\B=\C^{\gr}$ be the category of $\mathbb Z/2$-graded objects with the Koszul-signed braiding. It is the underlying category of the supercategory of Creutzig-Kanade-McRae. A supercommutative superalgebra $A=A_0\oplus A_1$ in $\C$ is the same
  as a commutative algebra $\bA$ in $\B$, and super-local modules are the local $\bA$-modules.
  Hence rigidity, pivotality and ribbon statements are instances of the ordinary theorems, with the ribbon condition $\theta_{A_0}=\id$, $\theta_{A_1}=\varepsilon\,\id$, where $\varepsilon=\pm1$ is fixed by the statistics of the odd part. For $\C$ non-degenerate and $\bA$ haploid and exact we prove
  that the category of super-local modules is a braided finite tensor category whose M\"uger center is $\mathsf{sVect}$. It is the centralizer of a fermion in a non-degenerate category obtained by condensing in $\C\boxtimes(\text{toric code})$. If $\C$ is ribbon and $\bA$ is symmetric Frobenius it is ribbon. We construct examples from graded simple currents, treat the free fermion and the symplectic fermion,
  and compare with Creutzig-Kanade-McRae and Creutzig-McRae-Shimizu-Yadav.

title: Complex Representatives, Similarity Invariants, and Iterates in $\bf{U(1,1;\mathbb{H})}$
authors: Bingzhe Hou, Cailing Yao, Jiaxing He
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24580v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the similarity classes of matrices in $U(1,1;\mathbb H)$ and the iterates of their associated quaternionic M\"obius transformations. Building on the known elliptic case, we show that every parabolic or loxodromic element of $U(1,1;\mathbb H)$ is similar, via a matrix in $U(1,1;\mathbb H)$, to a complex matrix. Explicit complex representatives and matrices realizing these similarities are constructed for the different types. We then introduce the invariants $\operatorname{Tr}(T), \Delta(T), \eta(T), \kappa(T)$, and prove that they form a complete system of similarity invariants for matrices in $U(1,1;\mathbb H)$. Finally, using the complex representation of quaternionic matrices and Chebyshev polynomials, we derive a fourth-order recurrence for a real sequence $(q_n)$ satisfying $\Delta(T^n)=q_n^2\Delta(T)$. Together with recurrence relations for the relevant matrix entries, this identity yields a complete classification of the quaternionic M\"obius transformation associated with $T^n$, including the degenerate cases in which $\Delta(T^n)=0$.

title: Local quadratic convergence of iterated correlation matrices: bounds and counterexamples
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24592v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Kruskal's unpublished manuscript on CONCOR gives a local argument for convergence of successive correlations to a prescribed two-class sign pattern. We identify a failure in its stated one-step estimate and establish a replacement bound for correlation matrices in arbitrary dimension. A geometric estimate for sign-aligned centered rows yields an explicit sufficient neighbourhood of convergence and a quadratic error bound. We construct invariant families of correlation matrices with an exact scalar recurrence in every dimension at least three. These families yield counterexamples to the original estimate in every dimension at least four. The failure persists on relatively open sets of positive-definite correlation matrices. In dimensions divisible by four, an explicitly solvable subfamily provides counterexamples arbitrarily close to the prescribed fixed point and attains the asymptotic coefficient in the new bound. Quadratic order is attained by the constructed families in every dimension at least three. These counterexamples concern the quantitative estimate, not the convergence conclusion: all the exhibited trajectories converge to their prescribed sign patterns.

title: Locally convex spaces with hemicompact weak* dual
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24615v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For a locally convex space $L$ let $L'_\sigma$ denote its dual endowed with the weak* topology $\sigma(L',L)$. We prove that $L'_\sigma$ is hemicompact if and only if $L$ with the Mackey topology $\tau(L,L')$ is metrizable and barrelled, and if and only if $L'_\sigma$ is $\sigma$-compact and quasi-complete. The key step is that a hemicompact $L'_\sigma$ is quasi-complete. The Mackey topology $\tau(L,L')$ is metrizable if and only if $L'$ is a countable union of absolutely convex weak*-compact sets; spaces with normable barrelled Mackey topology are characterized similarly. As a consequence, a metrizable (in particular, normed) space $L$ is barrelled if and only if $L'_\sigma$ is hemicompact. For function spaces we obtain: $(C_k(X))'_\sigma$ is hemicompact if and only if $X$ is hemicompact, and $(C_p(X))'_\sigma$ is hemicompact if and only if $X$ is countable and all compact subsets of $X$ are finite.

title: Optimal degree bounds for sum-of-squares representations
authors: Alexander Taveira Blomenhofer, Sander Gribling, Didier Henrion, Milan Korda, Poornendu Kumar, Victor Magron, Lucas Slot, Luis Felipe Vargas, Juan Vera
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24638v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The moment-sum-of-squares (SOS) hierarchy provides a sequence of bounds on the minimum of a polynomial over a basic closed semialgebraic set, i.e., a subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ defined by finitely many polynomial constraints. We establish optimal bounds on the error of the SOS hierarchy in the following settings:
  1. If the constraints define an Archimedean quadratic module: the error of the Putinar-based hierarchy at level $k$ is $\Theta((\log k)^4/k^2)$ in the worst case.
  2. If the constraints define a compact semialgebraic set: the error of the Schm\"udgen-based hierarchy at level $k$ is $\Theta((\log k)^2/k^2)$ in the worst case.
  3. If the constraints define an Archimedean quadratic module and satisfy linear independence constraint qualification conditions (LICQ): the error of the hierarchy at level $k$ is $\Theta(1/k^{4})$ in the worst case. Here, the upper bound holds already for the Putinar-based hierarchy, while the lower bound holds even against the Schm\"udgen-based hierarchy.
  Equivalently, these give best-possible effective versions of Putinar's and Schm\"udgen's Positivstellens\"atze for these settings (in terms of their dependence on $k$).

title: Unstable entropy for Anosov diffeomorphisms on tori isotopic to Anosov linear maps
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24647v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $f$ be an Anosov diffeomorphism on the $d$-torus which is strongly partially hyperbolic with expanding center. If $d=3$ or if $f$ is isotopic to its linear part, where the isotopy is contained in the set of partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms, we construct systems of strong-unstable and center-stable Margulis measures which are holonomy invariant. As a consequence, we obtain a characterization of measures of maximal unstable entropy in terms of their conditional measures along strong-unstable leaves. Moreover, we show that the unstable topological entropy, a measure of maximal unstable entropy and the Margulis system can be retrieved from the Pollicott-Ruelle spectrum of $f$.

title: Analytical Methods for Solving Non-Autonomous Higher-Order Nonlinear Difference Equations
authors: Tshifhiwa Murovhi, Mensah Folly-Gbetoula, Kwassi Anani
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24657v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A system of four-dimensional fifth-order rational difference equations with variable coefficients is considered. The method employed is the well-known Lie symmetry analysis initially developed for differential equations. Linearised symmetry conditions are applied, reduction operators are introduced, functional equations are solved, and symmetry generators are derived. The admitted point symmetries are then used to construct closed-form solutions. This work is a non-autonomous generalisation of autonomous fifth-order rational systems in the literature.

title: Numerical Analysis for a Nonlinear Coupled Thermoelastic System with Acoustic Boundary Conditions
authors: Adriano A. Alc\^antara, Bruno A. Carmo, Juan B. L\'imaco, Carlos M. Guzm\'an
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24704v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper presents the first $L^2$-norm error analysis for a nonlinear thermoelastic system with acoustic boundary conditions. The model involves three coupled variables: the acoustic potential $u$, the temperature $\theta$, and the normal displacement to the boundary $\delta$, with nonlinearities $|u|^d u$ in the domain and $g(\cdot,u')$ on the boundary, in addition to a nonlocal term $\beta(\int_\Omega\theta dx)\Delta\theta$ in the heat equation. We establish error estimates for the fully discrete problem, using the Crank-Nicolson method for time discretization and finite element method with basis of degree $r \geqslant 1$ for space discretization. We demonstrate that the domain-boundary coupling induces a half-power loss in the spatial convergence order for the variable $u$, and this effect propagates to the remaining variables due to the thermoelastic and boundary couplings, resulting in the final error estimate $\mathcal{O}(h^{r+\frac{1}{2}} + \tau^2)$. A bootstrap argument is employed to ensure the uniform boundedness of $\|U_h^n\|_{L^\infty}$, which is essential for handling the nonlinearity. Numerical results using Lagrange finite element basis of degrees $ r = 1, 2, 3 $ (linear, quadratic, and cubic) corroborate the theoretical estimates and illustrate the transition from suboptimal to optimal convergence orders when the exact solution possesses additional $L^\infty$ regularity.

title: Physical measures for partially hyperbolic systems with $u$-definite subbundles
abstract:
arXiv:2610.24743v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we study \(C^{1+\alpha}\) diffeomorphisms of a compact Riemannian manifold \(\mathbf{M}\) with an attracting set \(\Lambda\) admitting a partially hyperbolic splitting \[ T_\Lambda \mathbf{M} =
E^u\oplus C_1\oplus\cdots\oplus C_k\oplus E^s. \] We assume that, for every ergodic Gibbs \(u\)-state supported on \(\Lambda\), the Lyapunov exponents along each \(C_i\) are either all positive or all negative. We prove that \(\Lambda\) supports finitely many ergodic hyperbolic SRB measures whose basins cover Lebesgue almost every point of its topological basin.
  Our approach relies on an empirical basin-covering theorem for attracting sets with dominated splittings. Its proof hinges on a new notion of sliding suffix times, which allows us to synchronize expansion and contraction along a common empirical subsequence.
